about.title: Foster City Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products cause injuries everywhere, and Foster City residents are no exception — whether it's a faulty vehicle component involved in a crash along SR-92 or Foster City Boulevard, a malfunctioning household appliance, or an unsafe children's product. California's strict liability doctrine means an injured person generally doesn't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent, only that the product had a design flaw, manufacturing defect, or inadequate warning, and that this defect caused harm. Multiple parties along the supply chain — the manufacturer, distributor, and retailer — may share responsibility. Because San Mateo County sees hundreds of injury collisions each year, some tied to defective auto parts or tires, product liability issues can overlap with everyday crash claims. If you were hurt by a product in Foster City, preserving the item itself is critical to building a case. LawProactive offers a free way to get matched with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options, with no upfront cost.

items.title: Strict Liability Simplifies the Burden
items.desc: California generally allows injured people to pursue a claim by showing a product was defective and caused harm, without needing to prove the manufacturer acted carelessly. An attorney can help identify which type of defect applies to your situation.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable under California law. A connected attorney can help determine which parties were involved in getting the defective product into your hands.

items.title: Evidence Preservation Matters Early
items.desc: Since the product itself is often the central piece of evidence, acting quickly to preserve it can be important. LawProactive connects you with attorneys who can advise on next steps before evidence is lost or discarded.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. An attorney can assess whether your situation fits a design, manufacturing, or warning defect claim.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, including packaging, parts, or instructions. Avoid attempting repairs or discarding it, since it may serve as key evidence. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who can advise on proper handling.

items.question: Is this only about products found in stores, or could it involve a Foster City crash?
items.answer: Product liability can apply beyond household goods — for example, if a vehicle part like a tire or brake system failed during a crash along SR-92 or E Hillsdale Boulevard, that could point to a defective product issue rather than purely driver error. An independent attorney can help sort out whether a product defect contributed to the incident.
